items.title: Claude in Pharmaceutical Development: Real Lab Results and Real Errors
points: Anthropic acquired Mithril Medicine, a one-person biotech company that used Claude to develop a rare muscle disease treatment in 18 months with 11 outside labs—work typically requiring years and full teams.

Anthropic placed Claude in programs at six organizations including Bristol Myers Squibb and Generate Biomedicines, producing measurable gains: immune cells generated roughly 10 times more cancer-spotting receptors in lab-dish tests.
At Enveda, Claude reduced manufacturing chemist paperwork from 75% of their time to significantly less, while also catching 7 issues humans missed in QA reviews.

Mithril Medicine's Cody Tranbarger used Claude to coordinate contracts, logistics, and experiments across 11 labs for LAMA2-related congenital muscular dystrophy (a rare childhood muscle disease), completing mouse studies in under 18 months.

Mithril's own report documented six Claude errors, with at least three reaching outside labs via Claude-drafted emails that passed human editing—showing AI requires expert domain knowledge to catch mistakes before decisions are made.
All results remain preclinical (untested in humans); the mouse study was a pilot.

items.title: Google's Genie 4: Generative Worlds with Built-In Limitations
points: Google announced Genie 4, a generative AI that creates interactive game worlds with sound and characters that respond; typing commands like 'make it rain' mid-scene generates weather, sound, and character responses in real-time.
Access starts with trusted testers, then AI Ultra subscribers, then waitlist access, due to detail drift over time.
Google acknowledges 'detail drift'—objects and scene consistency degrade the longer a world runs, so a chair passed earlier may vanish if you turn back.
The model generates interactive sound alongside visuals, enabling characters to talk back within the generated environment.

items.title: Model Releases and Restrictions Reshape Open/Closed Competition
points: Mistral released a free 1-trillion-parameter open-weight model (Mistral Large 4) under a modified MIT license, tying GLM-5.3 as the top open-weight model for agentic coding (systems that chain AI calls to solve multi-step tasks).
Gemini 4 Carbon topped performance benchmarks, scoring 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, but access is restricted to Google's Fairwind cyber defense program (vetted defenders only).
Gemini 4 Carbon hallucinates (makes false claims) at 11%, up from 4% for the open Gemini 4 Argon version.
OpenAI began giving Pro and Business subscribers up to $500/month in API credits to build apps and agents, with unused credits expiring monthly.

items.title: Security and Enrollment Trends
points: Security researchers at Forever Security found five AI coding tools (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, VS Code, Claude Desktop) had hackable built-in browsers allowing unauthorized access; Cursor and Copilot shipped fixes, while Codex and VS Code remain unpatched.
US computer science undergraduate enrollment dropped 12.4% this fall while health majors grew 6.2%, per early figures from the National Student Clearinghouse.
